final_summary:
A 1-year-old girl presented with approximately 24 hours of right ear pain, irritability, crying, ear pulling, reduced feeding, and difficulty sleeping. She had no fever, vomiting, diarrhoea, respiratory symptoms, rash, or other systemic symptoms. Initial observations were normal and she was in no acute distress. Examination showed mild right auricular erythema and tenderness. Otoscopy demonstrated a bulging, erythematous right tympanic membrane with effusion; the left ear was normal. There was no mastoid tenderness, cellulitis, facial asymmetry, neurological deficit, lymphadenopathy, neck stiffness, or other evidence of systemic infection. The diagnosis was acute right otitis media with effusion, considered likely bacterial.

She was reviewed in the ED on 04/01/26 and remained clinically stable. Oral paracetamol 120 mg was given for pain. She was referred for paediatric/ENT inpatient review. Treatment was commenced with amoxicillin 125 mg/5 mL oral suspension, 2.5 mL three times daily for 5 days, and paracetamol 120 mg/5 mL, 5 mL four times daily as needed. Warm compresses and ear hygiene were advised. Pharmacy confirmed that the amoxicillin dose and 5-day course were appropriate, with no medication changes.

On ward review, she remained afebrile, alert, and without systemic infection. Parents reported significant overnight improvement in pain. Repeat otoscopy showed reduced right tympanic membrane erythema and effusion, and she tolerated oral medication without adverse effects. Discharge was planned with completion of the 5-day amoxicillin course, paracetamol as needed, warm compresses, and ENT follow-up in 2 weeks. The discharge plan was discussed with her GP, who was informed for continuity of care.
